tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use whenever a question involves...'), focuses on user-facing triggers (SPEKE, CPIX, DRM keys, error contracts, failure modes) rather than internal mechanics, explicitly covers edge cases ('even if DRM or SPEKE is not said'), and explicitly excludes out-of-scope areas with routing guidance. It is a dense but bounded paragraph, appropriate given the breadth of topics the skill covers.
tests.evidence: Use whenever a question involves SPEKE (v1/v2), CPIX, DRM content keys, encryption contracts, multi-key presets, DRM system IDs (Widevine/PlayReady/FairPlay), commonEncryptionScheme (cenc/cbcs/cbc1/cens), the key-rotation-vs-multi-key trade-off, player CENC/CBCS compatibility, the SPEKE v2 error contract, MediaPackage/MediaConvert encryption, or a DRM-layer failure... even if 'DRM' or 'SPEKE' is not said.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into AWS/SPEKE/DRM domain-specific facts (preset mappings, scheme values, error contracts) without re-explaining general concepts like what encryption or DRM is.
tests.evidence: `cbcs` -- AES-CBC, partial video-NAL pattern *(the cross-DRM CMAF default; FairPlay requires CBC-family)*

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed lookup tables (DRM UUIDs, trade-off table, v1 vs v2 table) are explicitly moved to references/lookup-tables.md and only linked from the body, with just short facts and summaries kept inline.
tests.evidence: Table: [Core facts to keep in context: DRM system UUIDs](references/lookup-tables.md#core-facts-to-keep-in-context-drm-system-uuids). Load it when you need the exact values.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ (cpix-authoring.md, lookup-tables.md, player-compatibility.md, presets-keys-security.md, providers.md, troubleshooting.md) has a markdown link in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies the exact condition under which it should be loaded (e.g., CPIX authoring, device compatibility questions, incident type).
tests.evidence: Load [references/player-compatibility.md](references/player-compatibility.md) for "this device won't play" questions: CENC vs CBCS support per platform, key-rotation support, fallback guidance.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative 'references/filename.md' format from the skill root with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile facts (scheme compatibility, rotation limitation, SL3000 rule) are stated as exact, prescriptive facts, while the architecture advisory mode is framed as a flexible decision tree allowing agent judgment based on context.
tests.evidence: Do not tell a user on MediaPackage v2 to "just set keyRotationIntervalSeconds" because "SPEKE v2 supports rotation." It will fail with UnprocessableEntityException.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where trade-offs exist (e.g., key rotation vs multi-key, scheme selection), the skill designates clear defaults/decision rules rather than listing options as equivalent.
tests.evidence: cbcs is the common choice when one CMAF endpoint must serve FairPlay + Widevine + PlayReady.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The architecture advisory and troubleshooting modes teach a generalizable decision-tree/diagnostic approach applicable to any DRM scenario, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Walk the decision tree, then state the concrete configuration: 1. Content value tier... 2. Target device footprint...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes substantial gotchas content inline (the rotation/multi-key trade-off, SL3000 audio-key rule, preset key-count misconception) that correct common misdiagnoses.
tests.evidence: This is the most common DRM misdiagnosis here.
